correctness.rationale: The twelve forms and marked coordinates agree with Dimca–Pokora–Sticlaru §5. The residue specialization is ω↦1, not reduction to the nonreduced ring R/(3). It gives −Q_t^9 r₁r₂r₃. The Hessian determinant of Q_t is (1−t)^3; the other determinants are nonzero scalar multiples of t. At A the inactive residual form has value 1−t³, and the gradients of Q_t,r₁,r₂ are (t−1)(1,t,t), (1,t,t), (1,t,t). In the chart z=1, substitution of x=ty² gives r₁=t(y−1)^3, exactly order three. At E_x the two residual conics have gradients in independent coordinate directions. This accounts for all four intersections of the pair by Bézout. Each Q_t–residual pair is tangent at two distinct points by symmetry, exhausting its Bézout sum with multiplicity two at each. The six singularities follow; the three smooth branches contribute pairwise sums 2+2+3, and the three nodes give total δ=24. Degree eight gives arithmetic genus 21. The labeled sections specialize as stated: (5.2) in the groups {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, {3,6,9}; (5.3) with labels 4,5,11 fixed at vertices and all other labels at (1:1:1), where the gradient of Q_t is (1−t)(1,1,1) and r_i=1−t. The latter assertion concerns the reduced support, not smoothness of the nonreduced divisor.
residual_risks: The frozen script was not executed. The checks are for the specified integral model at t≠0,1 and do not determine intrinsic singular-scheme lengths or a stable model.
